title: Application of a Mobile Device with LiDAR and a Laser Tracker in the Process of Building a Digital Twin of a Robotic Station
content: This article presents a procedure for preparing the geometric foundation of a digital twin of a robotic station planned for an existing production hall. The procedure combines environmental mapping using an Apple iPad Pro 13 equipped with LiDAR and the RobotStudio® AR Viewer application with the proposed use of a Leica AT960 tracker for reference measurements. The scan was saved in RSSCAN format, processed in RobotStudio and ATOS Professional, and integrated with the CAD design of the station. Of the six scans acquired, scans 5 and 6 were selected for a local comparison. Following rigid registration, the mean distance at ten points along a wall cross-section was 15.6 mm, the root mean square (RMS) distance was 19.3 mm, and the maximum was 39.1 mm. Following floor-prioritized registration, the corresponding values for ten points along a selected segment were 2.9 mm, 3.7 mm, and 8.4 mm. These results describe differences between the scans rather than accuracy relative to the hall; they also do not constitute a direct comparison of the two registration variants. A coordinate transformation model and an independent validation procedure were developed. The resulting scene supports a preliminary assessment of the station layout, whereas its use for robot programming requires reference measurements and validation after installation.
